title: Results

undefinedReason.fewerThanTwoObservations: The sample variance needs at least two valid observations.
undefinedReason.nonFiniteResult: The result cannot be represented in 64 bits.
undefinedReason.notEstimable: The parameter is not estimable (column is a combination of the others).
undefinedReason.noResidualDegreesOfFreedom: There are no error degrees of freedom (at least one group needs more than one observation).
undefinedReason.constantResponse: The response is constant: there is no variation to explain.
undefinedReason.noModelTerms: The model has no terms besides the intercept.
undefinedReason.zeroMean: The mean is zero: the coefficient of variation does not exist.

summary.evidence: Overall mean {{mean}} and standard deviation {{sd}}{{unit}}; see the table by group.
summary.evidenceUndefined: Not every overall statistic could be calculated; see the reasons in the table.
summary.nextStepGroups: Group means describe the data but do not show whether the groups differ. That decision needs a comparison test (ANOVA and Tukey), which has not been delivered yet.
summary.nextStepNoGroups: To compare conditions, add a factor and group by it; the comparison test (ANOVA and Tukey) has not been delivered yet.

stale: The data or options changed after this calculation. Calculate again to update the result.

descriptive.no_valid_observations: No valid observation for this response.
descriptive.independence_not_assessed: n counts observations. The app does not assume they are independent replicates: that depends on how the experiment was run.
descriptive.missing_excluded_one: {{count}} observation without a value was counted as missing and did not enter the mean, variance, minimum or maximum.
descriptive.missing_excluded_other: {{count}} observations without a value were counted as missing and did not enter the mean, variance, minimum or maximum.
descriptive.excluded_missing_factor_one: {{count}} observation with no value in some grouping factor is outside the groups (but counts in the overall summary).
descriptive.excluded_missing_factor_other: {{count}} observations with no value in some grouping factor are outside the groups (but count in the overall summary).
descriptive.group_too_small_one: Group “{{group}}” has {{count}} valid observation; variance and standard deviation need at least two.
descriptive.group_too_small_other: Group “{{group}}” has {{count}} valid observations; variance and standard deviation need at least two.

anova.significant: The F test detected a difference among group means (F({{df1}}, {{df2}}) = {{f}}; p = {{p}}; α = {{alpha}}). It does not say which groups differ.
anova.not_significant: The F test did not detect a difference among means (F({{df1}}, {{df2}}) = {{f}}; p = {{p}}; α = {{alpha}}). Failing to detect a difference does not prove the means are equal.

tukey.pairs_different: Tukey: {{count}} of {{total}} pairs differ at α = {{alpha}} (family of all pairwise mean comparisons).
tukey.kramer: Group sizes differ: the Tukey–Kramer extension was used.

letters.meaning: Groups sharing a letter showed no detected difference; this does not mean they are equivalent.
letters.unknown_pairs: Some pairs could not be tested and were treated as different when assigning letters.

diagnostics.homogeneity_signal: Brown–Forsythe indicates unequal variances among groups (p = {{p}}). Compare the standard deviations and the residual plot; the app does not switch methods automatically.
diagnostics.homogeneity_not_detected: Brown–Forsythe did not detect a difference in variances (p = {{p}}); this does not guarantee homogeneity.
diagnostics.normality_visual: Normality of the residuals should be judged on the quantile–quantile plot; there is no automatic validity badge.
diagnostics.independence_not_assessed: The app does not check independence: each row was treated as an independent observation. Repeated measurements of the same experimental unit are not replicates.
diagnostics.outliers_one: {{count}} standardised residual exceeds 3 in absolute value: check that observation in the plots.
diagnostics.outliers_other: {{count}} standardised residuals exceed 3 in absolute value: check those observations in the plots.

comparison.singleton_groups_one: {{count}} group has a single observation: it has no standard deviation or interval, but it enters the ANOVA.
comparison.singleton_groups_other: {{count}} groups have a single observation: they have no standard deviation or interval, but they enter the ANOVA.
comparison.excluded_observations_one: {{count}} observation was left out for a missing response or factor level.
comparison.excluded_observations_other: {{count}} observations were left out for a missing response or factor level.

design.saturated: There are no error degrees of freedom (the model uses every run): standard errors, t tests and p-values do not exist.
design.no_inference: No estimable error and too few effects for Lenth's method: only effect magnitudes can be compared.
design.lenth_only: Active effects come from Lenth's method, which is approximate; treat it as a clue, not a test.
design.no_active_effects: No term was flagged as active at level {{alpha}}.
design.aliased_active: Note: {{terms}} is aliased with other effects in this design; the estimate is their sum.
design.curvature_detected: Curvature detected (p = {{p}}): the linear model does not describe the region well; consider a design with quadratic terms.
design.curvature_not_detected: Curvature not detected (p = {{p}}); this does not prove the response is linear.
design.curvature_unavailable: Curvature could not be tested with these data.
design.lack_of_fit_significant: Significant lack of fit (p = {{p}}): the chosen model leaves systematic variation out.
design.screening_pb: Plackett–Burman is a resolution III screening design: main effects are partially aliased with two-factor interactions.
design.unexpected_levels: {{count}} runs have levels other than low, high or centre; the fit uses the coded values of those rows.
design.independence_not_assessed: The app does not check independence: each row was treated as an independent run.
design.not_estimable_one: {{count}} term is not estimable (aliased with another in the model) and was left out.
design.not_estimable_other: {{count}} terms are not estimable (aliased with others in the model) and were left out.

surface.model_significant: The model is significant at the {{alpha}} level (p = {{p}}).
surface.model_not_significant: The model is not significant at the {{alpha}} level (p = {{p}}): the surface cannot be told apart from a constant response.
surface.saturated: There are no error degrees of freedom (the model uses every run): standard errors, tests and p-values do not exist.
surface.lack_of_fit_significant: There is lack of fit (p = {{p}}): the second-order model does not describe the studied region well; consider a smaller region or additional terms.
surface.lack_of_fit_unavailable: Lack of fit could not be assessed: runs must be repeated at the same conditions (for example, the centre point).
surface.not_estimable: {{count}} term(s) not estimable with these runs; the design cannot separate them.
surface.extrapolation_note: Predictions outside the region run (hatched in the charts) are extrapolation and are not reliable.
surface.independence_not_assessed: Independence of the runs cannot be checked from the data; it depends on how the experiment was run.

optimization.no_global_claim: The search is local with many starts: it does not prove that the best candidate is the global optimum.
optimization.infeasible: No candidate satisfies the mandatory limits in the searched region.
optimization.zero_desirability: Global desirability is zero at every feasible point found: at least one goal cannot be met together with the others.
optimization.single_start: The best solution came from a single start: increase the number of starts to check whether better solutions exist.
optimization.boundary: The best solution is at the domain limit for: {{factors}}. The optimum may lie beyond, outside the experimental region.
optimization.extrapolated: {{count}} candidate(s) outside the experimental region (extrapolation): treat them with caution.
optimization.compromise: With several responses there are trade-offs: see how much each response gives up relative to the best it would reach alone.
optimization.confirm_with_runs: Predictions come from the model: confirm candidates with new runs before adopting them.

summary.conclusion: Compared {{groups}} groups of “{{factor}}” using {{n}} observations of “{{response}}”.
summary.evidenceDefined: ANOVA: F({{df1}}, {{df2}}) = {{f}}, p = {{p}}. Tukey: {{different}} of {{total}} pairs differ (α = {{alpha}}).
summary.evidenceUndefined: ANOVA could not be computed with these data; see the warnings below.
summary.nextStepWithLetters: Read the letters on the chart: groups with no letter in common differ; groups sharing a letter showed no detected difference. Check the pairs table and the diagnostics before concluding.
summary.nextStepNoLetters: There are no error degrees of freedom (replicates within groups) to compare pairs. Add independent replicates.

effects.eta: η² (share of total variation explained by the factor)

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.ratio: Ratio of the largest to the smallest group standard deviation: {{ratio}}

charts.se: Standard error of the group mean
charts.meansDescription: Bar chart with each group's mean, uncertainty bars and comparison letters.
charts.uncertaintySe: Bars: mean ± standard error of the group mean
charts.uncertaintyCi: Bars: mean ± {{level}}% CI (pooled variance, Student t)
charts.lettersLegend: Shared letters = difference not detected (Tukey, α = {{alpha}}); not evidence of equivalence.
charts.boxDescription: Boxplot of each group with median, quartiles, whiskers and far points.
charts.boxLegend: Box: 1st to 3rd quartile; bar: median; whiskers: up to 1.5 × interquartile range; circles: far points.
charts.residualsDescription: Standardised residuals against the group mean; look for scatter with no pattern.
charts.residualsLegend: A funnel, curvature or isolated points suggest unequal variance or model problems.
charts.qqDescription: Ordered standardised residuals against theoretical normal quantiles.
charts.qqLegend: Points near the (quartile) line suggest roughly normal residuals; also use knowledge of the experiment.
charts.tableHint: The pairs table below lists every comparison in the chart.

export.title: Export
export.failed: The file could not be exported.

summary.conclusion: Analysed {{n}} runs of “{{response}}” with {{factors}} factors (model with {{terms}} terms).
summary.evidenceLenth: No error degrees of freedom: by Lenth's method (indicative), active terms: {{active}}.
summary.evidenceUnavailable: No inference is available with these data; see the warnings.
summary.nextStep: Screening points to candidates, not optimal values: confirm the active factors in a new experiment (for example, response surface) and check the aliasing before concluding.

effects.caption: Effects and coefficients (coded scale) for “{{response}}”
effects.help: The coefficient is the change per coded unit; the effect is the difference between the high and low level means. Without error degrees of freedom there is no standard error or p-value.

curvature.title: Curvature
curvature.text: Difference between the centre points and the linear model's prediction: {{difference}} (t = {{t}}, p = {{p}}; {{points}} centre points).
curvature.unavailable: Curvature not tested: no error degrees of freedom or no centre points.

lackOfFit.title: Lack of fit and pure error
lackOfFit.text: Pure error: SS {{ssPure}} with {{dfPure}} df; lack of fit: SS {{ssLof}} with {{dfLof}} df; F = {{f}}, p = {{p}}.
lackOfFit.noTest: Lack of fit: SS {{ssLof}} with {{dfLof}} df; no F test available.

lenth.title: Lenth's method
lenth.text: Pseudo standard error (PSE) {{pse}}, {{df}} df; margin of error {{me}}, simultaneous margin {{sme}}. Effects with |effect| above the margin are flagged as active.
lenth.help: Indicative, not an exact test: it assumes most effects are zero.

charts.paretoDescription: Horizontal bars in decreasing order with a reference line.
charts.paretoLegendT: Bars beyond the line: terms with p < α. Non-estimable terms are not shown.
charts.paretoLegendLenth: No error degrees of freedom: the line is Lenth's margin of error (indicative).
charts.paretoLegendEffect: No estimable error: only the effect magnitudes, with no reference line.
charts.mainDescription: Mean response at the low and high level of each factor.
charts.interactionDescription: Mean response at combinations of two factors' levels.
charts.mainLegend: Line: mean response at the low and high levels; square: mean of the centre points. In fractional designs the means reflect the aliasing.
charts.interactionLegend: Non-parallel lines suggest an interaction. In fractional designs the means reflect the aliasing.
charts.opDescription: Observed values against the model's predictions, with the y = x line.
charts.opLegend: Points near the line indicate a good fit; systematic departures indicate lack of fit.

summary.conclusion: Second-order model fitted to {{n}} runs of “{{response}}” with {{factors}} factors ({{terms}} terms).
summary.evidence: Regression ANOVA: F = {{f}}, p = {{p}}; R² = {{r2}}; adjusted R² = {{adjusted}}.
summary.evidenceUnavailable: Without error degrees of freedom there are no tests; see the warnings.
summary.nextStep: The model describes only the studied region. Check lack of fit and the residuals before using the equation, and confirm any promising point with new runs.

terms.caption: Model coefficients (coded scale) for “{{response}}”
terms.help: Coefficients are on the coded scale (−1 and +1 at the stated levels): they can be compared with one another regardless of units.

lackOfFit.unavailable: Lack of fit unavailable: there are no repeated runs at the same conditions (pure error) or not enough degrees of freedom. Repeat the centre point to test it.

equation.title: Model equation
equation.realUnavailable: Unavailable: some terms are not estimable.
equation.help: Both equations give the same prediction; the coded one is the one fitted and the real one is the same equation rewritten in the factor values.

region.title: Experimental region
region.help: Predictions outside the region, or at level combinations never run, are extrapolation.

view.title: Response surface
view.intro: Choose two factors for the axes and fix the others. Predictions come from the model; the hatched region is extrapolation.
view.sameAxis: Choose different factors on the two axes.
view.failed: The grid could not be computed.
view.contourDescription: Contour lines of the response predicted by the model as a function of two factors.
view.surfaceDescription: Surface of the response predicted by the model as a function of two factors, in orthographic projection.
view.readingContour: Lines: predicted response values; darker = higher response.
view.points: Circles: runs, projected on the two axes.
view.needTwo: The surface needs at least two quantitative factors.

export.title: Export and figure appearance
export.intro: Choose the language of the files, the CSV table format and the figure style. Tables and figures can also be downloaded with the buttons next to each one.
export.deviceNote: These preferences apply to this device and are recorded in the metadata of exported files; they are not saved in the project.

report.title: Report
report.subtitle: Report generated by EnziTAG Optima: method, configuration, tables, figures and interpretation.
report.footer: EnziTAG Optima {{version}} — self-contained file, generated locally.
report.footerPdf: EnziTAG Optima {{version}} — PDF generated locally; figures are vector graphics.

export.logo: Include the group logo in reports

figure.title: Title
figure.help: Changes appearance only. The setting is saved in the project, applies to the screen and to exported files, and changes no result.
figure.manualLettersHelp: One per group, in chart order, separated by spaces; use - to leave a group without a letter. When filled in, they replace the computed ones in the figure only (the table does not change).
figure.manualLettersLegend: Letters typed manually (not computed by the app).
figure.annotationHelp: Position as a percentage of the figure (0 = left/top, 100 = right/bottom).

model.title: Model: terms and comparison
model.intro: Clear a term to remove it from the model (for example, the quadratic effect of a factor); the app recalculates and compares the models.
model.confirmHierarchy: Removing this term leaves an interaction or a quadratic term of the same factor in the model, which breaks model hierarchy. Continue?
model.metricsHelp: Adjusted R² and predicted R² penalize unnecessary terms; lower AICc and BIC indicate a better balance between fit and simplicity. No single metric decides: the choice is yours.

stopped.no_candidate: The sequence stops here: no remaining term has a p-value above α.
stopped.hierarchy: The sequence stops here: the remaining terms with a high p-value are needed to keep the hierarchy.
stopped.no_degrees_of_freedom: The sequence stops here: too few residual degrees of freedom would remain.

model.warnLackOfFit: Significant lack of fit: the current model may be too simple for these data.
model.warnFewDf: Only {{df}} residual degrees of freedom remain: error estimates are unreliable.
model.warnOverfit: Predicted R² is well below adjusted R²: a sign of overfitting. Prefer a simpler model.
model.optimism: P-values computed after choosing terms from the same data are optimistic. Confirm the final model with new runs.
model.responseHelp: Each response keeps its own model; the optimization uses the model chosen for each one.

procedure.title: Treatment comparison
procedure.pairsHelp: The adjusted p-value already accounts for the family of comparisons. Sharing a letter does not prove equivalence: it only means the difference was not detected.
procedure.controlNote: Each treatment is compared only with the control ({{control}}); there are no letters.

explain.gamesHowell: Does not assume equal variances: uses Welch's ANOVA and, for each pair, Welch–Satterthwaite degrees of freedom with the studentized range.
explain.dunnett: Compares each treatment only with the control, controlling the family error with the exact distribution of the maximum of the t statistics.
explain.bonferroni: t tests between all pairs with the pooled variance; p-values are multiplied by the number of comparisons.
explain.holm: t tests between all pairs with the pooled variance; Holm adjustment, always at least as powerful as Bonferroni.
explain.kruskalDunn: Rank-based method, no normality assumption; ties receive the average rank and enter the correction.

global.welch_anova: Welch's ANOVA: F = {{stat}} ({{df1}} and {{df2}} d.f.), p = {{p}}.
global.anova: One-way ANOVA: F = {{stat}} ({{df1}} and {{df2}} d.f.), p = {{p}}.
